rule.title: Future continuous: will be + -ing
rule.explanation:
El future continuous («will be» + «-ing») describe una acción que estará en marcha en un momento del futuro:
- «This time tomorrow we'll be walking around Dublin.» (mañana a esta hora estaremos paseando por Dublín)
- «At ten I'll be flying over France.»

También se usa para planes que van a pasar en el curso normal de las cosas, y para preguntar por planes con educación:
- «I'll be seeing Helen at the meeting anyway.»
- «Will you be using the car tonight?» (¿vas a usar el coche esta noche?)

La negativa es «won't be» + «-ing»:
- «I won't be working on Friday.»

Compáralo con «will» + verbo, que es una acción puntual:
- «The plane will land at twelve.»
- «At twelve we'll be landing.» (en pleno aterrizaje)

Ojo: los verbos de estado no van en continuous tampoco aquí: «I'll be at home» (nunca «I'll be being»), «I'll know tomorrow».

rows: This time tomorrow I'll be flying.
Will you be using the car?
I won't be working on Friday.
The plane will land at twelve.

sets.instructions: Completa con el future continuous («will be» + «-ing») del verbo entre paréntesis.

items.sentence: This time tomorrow we'll be ___ around Dublin. (walk)
Don't call at eleven. I'll ___ flying. (be)
Maureen will be ___ for us at the station. (wait)
I ___ be working at Easter. I'm on holiday! (negativa)
___ you be checking in any bags?
At midnight we'll ___ sleeping in the hotel. (be)
At ten o'clock I ___ a presentation. (give)
Will you ___ using the car tonight?
In a year, Javi will be ___ in Dublin. (live)
Don't worry about the plants. I'll be ___ after them. (look)
We ___ dinner at eight, so come at nine. (have)
This time next week I'll ___ lying on a beach. (be)
The plane ___ land at twelve. (acción puntual)
Will you be ___ Helen at the meeting? (see)
